newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Light grades see limited improvement.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Light grades see limited improvement.

text.p: Asia's light crude market was steady, but deals done at wide discounts dashed sellers' hopes of a stronger market in August.
A Cossack cargo for second half August was sold on Monday to an Australian refiner at Tapis APPI -$1.00 per barrel.
A major last week had sold an August Kutubu to China at Tapis APPI -70, which kept the market optimistic that levels were moving higher.
But some traders were surprised that China was willing to pay a firmer level for the crude when recent deals had been done at discounts of more than $1.00 to Tapis APPI.
But the latest Cossack trade and the Tapis cargo sold at a discount to APPI has caused uncertainty, with traders waiting for the next deal to get a clearer idea of market direction.

Several cargoes of Cossack, Kutubu and New Zealand's Maui condensate were heard available for August, with demand expected to be thin as Australia's Ampol, the largest buyer of light crudes, was planning a maintenance shutdown of its 40,000 crude distillation unit at its Lytton refinery in August.
Ampol covers 90 percent of its crude requirements with regional light sweets, mainly Cossack and Kutubu.
Refiners said that the delay in the start up of the Griffin field after maintenance was unlikely to tighten supplies.
"There hasn't been any Griffin available since April, so I don't think the lack of Griffin supplies in August is a bullish factor," said a refiner in Australia.
Trading on the heavy Asian crudes was quiet, with most traders waiting for the outcome Indonesian August allocations, due out this week.
In the Middle East, August Masila was done at Dubai +8/9 cents to South Korea. --A. Ahmad, Singapore (+65 870 3082)
